newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ ManFed against higher government spending.
newsitem.headline: NZ ManFed against higher government spending.

text.p: Increased government spending would lead to higher interest rates and a stronger New Zealand dollar, the Manufacturers Federation said on Thursday.
"This will mean exports and jobs will suffer," federation Chief Executive Simon Arnold said in a statement.
Arnold's statement was in response to comments from New Zealand First Party leader Winston Peters that increased spending was inevitable.

"It will also mean we are in for a glum Christmas as mortgage owners find they have less disposable income and reduced spending flows through to less returns for retailers and producers," Arnold said.
Peters holds the balance of power while coalition talks continue after an inconclusive general election on October 12.
Arnold said exporters and manufacturers were becoming concerned at the lack of apparent progress in the negotiations.
